title: Inverse cosine values and a sum rewritten as a single sine term

stimulus.title: Inverse cosine and a single sine term
stimulus.text: No calculator. Give exact values, use radians, and show the work for each part. Only real solutions are asked for.

table.caption: The expressions and equations in this question, by part

parts.label: A(i)
parts.sample: Let $\theta = \cos^{-1}\left(-\frac{3}{5}\right)$, an angle in $[0, \pi]$ with $\cos\theta = -\frac{3}{5}$, so $\theta$ is in Quadrant II. $\sin^2\theta = 1 - \frac{9}{25} = \frac{16}{25}$, and sine is positive in Quadrant II, so $\sin\theta = \frac{4}{5}$.

parts.label: B
parts.prompt: Rewrite $k(x) = \sin\left(x + \frac{\pi}{6}\right) + \sin\left(x - \frac{\pi}{6}\right)$ as a single term of the form $a\sin x$. Show the identities you use.

rubric.point: Expands both with the sum and difference identities for sine

parts.sample: $\sin\left(x + \frac{\pi}{6}\right) = \sin x\cos\frac{\pi}{6} + \cos x\sin\frac{\pi}{6}$ and $\sin\left(x - \frac{\pi}{6}\right) = \sin x\cos\frac{\pi}{6} - \cos x\sin\frac{\pi}{6}$. Adding, the cosine terms cancel: $k(x) = 2\sin x\cos\frac{\pi}{6} = 2\cdot\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\sin x = \sqrt{3}\sin x$.

parts.label: C

rubric.point: Uses part B to get $\sin x = \frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}$ and gives one correct solution
Both solutions $x = \frac{\pi}{3}$ and $x = \frac{2\pi}{3}$, and no others

parts.sample: By part B, $\sqrt{3}\sin x = \frac{3}{2}$, so $\sin x = \frac{3}{2\sqrt{3}} = \frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}$. In $[0, 2\pi)$ this gives $x = \frac{\pi}{3}$ and, by symmetry, $x = \pi - \frac{\pi}{3} = \frac{2\pi}{3}$.
